title: Roberts v. New River Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint sustained. The SJC answered yes that New River Presbytery erred at its November 8–9, 1991 meeting by not accepting TE Don Post Jr.'s resignation and dissolving his pastoral relation. The SJC approved the majority panel judgment 16 concurring, 3 dissenting. No remand or further directive appears in the adopted judgment, and the Presbytery had already dissolved the relation on December 7, 1991. The dissents would have found the complaint in order but denied.
first_summary: A congregation member complained that New River Presbytery erred in November 1991 by not immediately accepting TE Don Post Jr.'s resignation and dissolving his pastoral relation. The SJC reversed the Presbytery's denial and remanded for dissolution. It held BCO 23-1 required acceptance because the congregation concurred and no sufficient reasons to retain him appeared; BCO 13-9 did not override that specific rule. Three commissioners dissented.
summary: A congregation member complained that New River Presbytery erred in November 1991 by declining to accept TE Don Post Jr.'s resignation and dissolve his pastoral relation, instead appointing a commission. The SJC sustained the complaint. Under BCO 23-1, once the congregation concurred and no sufficient reasons to retain the pastor appeared, the resignation 'shall be accepted' and the relation dissolved; the Presbytery's general BCO 13-9 power did not override that specific provision. The Presbytery had already dissolved the relation on December 7, 1991; the adopted judgment ordered no remand. Three commissioners dissented.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Case 1992-02 / Judicial Case 92-2, Roberts v. New River Presbytery. SJC majority judgment approved 16 concurring, 3 dissenting, lines 9–60, printed pp. 199–201. Source path/hash as supplied.
evidence_notes.dispute: RE Virgil B. Roberts complained on Nov. 25, 1991 that New River Presbytery failed to adopt the motion accepting TE Don Post Jr.'s resignation and dissolving the pastoral relation at its Nov. 8–9 meeting. Presbytery found the complaint in order but denied it Dec. 7; complaint filed with SJC Dec. 23. Lines 18–39, printed pp. 200–201.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: SJC answered the issue yes: BCO 23-1 required acceptance and dissolution when the congregation appeared and reasons to retain the pastor were insufficient; the Shepherding Committee had opportunity and raised no objection; no record basis appeared for the commission. BCO 13-9 general powers could not override specific BCO 23-1. Lines 41–58, printed pp. 201–202; vote line 60.
evidence_notes.qualifications: The adopted judgment contains no remand or further proceedings order. Presbytery had already dissolved the relation on Dec. 7, 1991. The two dissents, lines 62–211, argue the complaint should be denied but are separate opinions, not the adopted holding.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: The majority cites prior case 91-2 for the proposition that BCO 23-1 discretion does not give a presbytery power to prevent implementation of a valid congregational decision, including concurrence in resignation; the prior decision is cited as precedent, not reproduced or incorporated. Lines 58, printed p. 202.

source_limits: Source supplies the full majority judgment, reasoning, vote, and two dissents, but no complaint, briefs, minutes, or full text of cited case 91-2. The adopted judgment gives no explicit remedy beyond sustaining the complaint.
benchmark_examples: C01 (Allin v. Tennessee Valley Presbytery): preserve each material successful and unsuccessful issue and the actual remedy; here the complaint is sustained, but no remand appears in the adopted judgment.
C20 (Daniels v. Nashville Presbytery): unexplained dispositions must remain unexplained; this adopted ruling, by contrast, states its BCO 23-1 reasoning.

score_reasons.concrete_dispute: Identifies Presbytery's November 1991 refusal to accept the resignation/dissolve the relation and its appointment of a commission instead.
score_reasons.decision: States that the complaint was sustained, the 16–3 vote, the absence of a remand order, and the separate dissents.
score_reasons.decisive_reason: Explains the adopted BCO 23-1 requirement and the specific-over-general reasoning against BCO 13-9.
score_reasons.distinctive_value: Preserves the rule that general presbytery powers do not override BCO 23-1 and notes the reliance on prior case 91-2.
score_reasons.fidelity: Separates the adopted SJC judgment from the Presbytery's earlier denial and from the dissenting opinions.
score_reasons.economy: Focuses on the challenged action, adopted rule, relief or limit, and dissent without importing dissent details or historical background.

Also confirmed the Presbytery had already dissolved the relation on Dec. 7, 1991, that the SJC vote was 16 concurring and 3 dissenting, and that the commission finding against the Session was not approved by Presbytery.
